title: Intrinsic anomalous Hall effect in the surface conduction regime of non-magnetic narrow-gap insulator FeSi
authors: Yong-Cheng Pan, Hwai-Chi Lin, Li-Han Wang, Chia-Nung Kuo, Han-Shiuan Lin, Che-Ning Yeh, Chin-Shan Lue, Anne de Visser, Yu-Te Hsu
abstract: The realization of an intrinsic anomalous Hall effect (AHE) in the absence of bulk magnetism is a rare phenomenon, requiring a spontaneous breaking of the time-reversal symmetry within the boundary states without a thermodynamic phase transition. Here, we report a robust, zero-field-hysteretic intrinsic AHE confined to the low-temperature surface-conduction regime of the prototypical narrow-gap insulator FeSi. By systematically investigating single crystals grown via Czochralski and chemical vapor transport methods with controlled thicknesses and surface preparations, we demonstrate that low-temperature electrical conductivity correlates with surface roughness and anti-correlates with sample thickness, confirming the emergence of surface conducting states (CSS) below $T_{\rm CSS} \simeq 55-75\text{ K}$. Meanwhile, a robust, field-hysteretic and temperature-independent anomalous Hall conductivity is found below $T_{\rm AHE}\simeq45-70\text{ K}$, implying the presence of magnetic order in the surface conduction regime. Bulk magnetic susceptibility and specific-heat measurements reveal no thermodynamic phase transitions, verifying that the sample interior remains a non-magnetic insulator. Analyses of conductivity scaling and effective three-dimensional conductivity reveal the intrinsic nature of this surface-driven AHE, evidencing the presence of an emergent magnetic order within the metallic surface of a non-magnetic bulk insulator. These findings establish FeSi as a compelling platform to investigate the interplay between strong electron correlations and anomalous Hall transport.
summary: This work reports the discovery of an intrinsic anomalous Hall effect in the surface conduction layer of the non-magnetic insulator FeSi. By correlating the AHE onset with the emergence of surface conducting states, the authors argue for the existence of an emergent, surface-confined magnetic order. This establishes FeSi as a key platform for studying the interplay between strong correlations and anomalous transport phenomena.
main_problem: The research investigates the rare phenomenon of observing an intrinsic anomalous Hall effect (AHE) in a material that lacks bulk magnetism, suggesting surface-confined symmetry breaking.
main_result: The authors report a robust, field-hysteretic intrinsic AHE confined to the surface conduction regime of the non-magnetic insulator FeSi, indicating emergent magnetic order at the surface.
method: The study combines systematic single-crystal growth, low-temperature magnetotransport measurements (Hall and longitudinal resistivity), and thermodynamic characterization (susceptibility and specific heat).
model_or_system: The physical system is the non-magnetic narrow-gap insulator FeSi. The focus is on the electronic properties of the surface conduction states (CSS) that emerge at low temperatures.
key_observables: Anomalous Hall conductivity ($\sigma_{Axy}$), low-temperature electrical conductivity ($\sigma_{xx}$), magnetic susceptibility ($\chi(T)$), and specific heat ($C/T$).
important_parameters: Low temperatures ($T_{AHE} \simeq 45-70 	ext{ K}$), surface roughness ($R_q$), and sample thickness.
main_assumptions: The AHE is intrinsic and surface-driven, confirmed by conductivity scaling, and the bulk material remains non-magnetic despite surface magnetism.
figures_summary: Figures show normalized resistance vs. T for different sample types, Hall resistivity ($ho_{xy}$) vs. applied field isotherms demonstrating hysteresis, and $\sigma_{Axy}(T)$ tracking the CSS temperature scale.
paper_structure: The paper systematically presents evidence for surface conduction states (CSS) via thickness/roughness dependence, followed by the observation of a robust, hysteretic AHE confined to this surface regime, while simultaneously ruling out bulk magnetic origins via thermodynamic measurements.
why_interesting: The observation of intrinsic AHE without bulk magnetism provides a clean platform to study emergent magnetic order driven purely by surface electronic structure, which is relevant to understanding topological surface states and symmetry breaking in correlated systems.
